summary: Flathead NF summit 20 miles northwest of Polebridge; a 1930s cabin near the Canadian border is listed abandoned, but a 2016 article describes a fire lookout on top, so the sources disagree.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts says the 1930s cabin was abandoned; a 2016 Wildsight article describes a fire lookout on top of Mt. Hefty

access.note: Reached by trail #15 from the Thoma-Colts Creek (#18) trailhead; the trip report says a ranger told hikers the Forest Service no longer maintained the northern part of trail #15

visit.trail_note: About 2.6 miles from the #18 trailhead to the trail #15 junction; the 2016 article lists a 15.6 km round trip of about 3 hours

evidence.supports: 1930s cabin about a quarter mile south of the Canadian border; listed as abandoned
evidence.quote: 1930s: cabin 1/4 mile south of Canadian border. Abandoned.

evidence.supports: location in the Flathead National Forest
twin summits straddle the U.S.-Canada border
2016 article describes a fire lookout on top of Mt. Hefty
evidence.quote: Looking east from the fire lookout on top of Mt. Hefty

evidence.supports: a ranger told hikers the Forest Service no longer maintained the northern part of trail #15
evidence.quote: the National Forest Service no longer maintained the northern part of trail #15 to Mt. Hefty

evidence.supports: hike starts at the Thoma-Colts Creek (#18) trailhead
evidence.quote: we finally arrived at the Thoma-Colts Creek (#18) trailhead

evidence.supports: about 2.6 miles from the #18 trailhead to the trail #15 junction
evidence.quote: From the #18 trailhead, it was about 2.6 miles to the intersection with the Mt. Hefty Trail (#15).

evidence.supports: 2016 article lists a 15.6 km round trip of about three hours

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts says the 1930s cabin was abandoned, which does not show that nothing stands; a 2016 Wildsight article describes a fire lookout on top of Mt. Hefty.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the 1930s cabin was abandoned; Wildsight's 2016 article describes a fire lookout on the summit. We could not tell whether these are the same structure or a later one.

notes_for_editor: Thin sources and a real conflict: the Forest Lookouts page says abandoned, the 2016 Wildsight article describes a lookout on top. The trip report and the Wildsight piece are not dated in our copies. Elevation (Forest Lookouts 7585 ft) is not used. No staffing or fire history found. A recent photo or a Flathead NF records check would settle the summit question.
